newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Littlewoods shops eyed by foodstores.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Littlewoods shops eyed by foodstores.

text.p: Britain's leading food retailer Tesco Plc and value-for-money ASDA Group Plc were tipped by analysts on Tuesday as favourites to buy the 135 shops put up for sale by private company Littlewoods LWD.CN.
"In my view there are two candidates, Tesco and ASDA," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
Littlewoods wants to sell the stores, estimated to be worth around 500 million pounds ($800 million), to focus on its mail order and football pools leisure businesses.
Chairman James Ross told Reuters that potential buyers had already made approaches and said that food retailers could be among those interested.
"The market is saying it expects Tesco and ASDA to be among the bidders," one sector analyst said.
In a rising market, Tesco shares remained flat at 340-1/2 pence by 1344 GMT while ASDA was down a smidgeon at 111-1/2 pence.
ASDA was not immediately available for comment while a spokeswoman for Tesco said it never commented on market speculation.
"Food retailers will assume that they can increase turnover substantially," the analyst said.
He estimated current turnover at Littlewoods stores to be around 3.50 pounds per square foot in a week, compared with nearer 18-20 pounds for superstores.
Littlewoods said on Tuesday that total group turnover was 2.28 billion pounds for the year to December 31, 1996, with pretax profits up 15 percent to 112.1 million pounds.
Analysts said on top of the potential to boost sales, attractions would then differ between Tesco and ASDA.
For ASDA, the stores could present a welcome opportunity to expand its non-food operations such as its George clothing line, exclusive to ASDA stores.

ASDA Chief Executive Allan Leighton has said he wants the George brand, headed by George Davies who founded the Next chain of fashion stores, to be number two in the market behind the household name of high street giant Marks & Spencer.
Tesco, meanwhile, might want to expand its Tesco Metro high street outlets which it launched to complement its larger out-of-town superstore portfolio, analysts said.
The supermarket might decide to rent out floor space or whole stores which were unacceptable for the Tesco Metro format, analysts added.
"The Littlewoods stores could also be seen as a property portfolio," the sector analyst said.
Neither of the other two major supermarkets were considered likely buyers.
J. Sainsbury Plc was thought unlikely to go shopping for more stores while its existing ones struggle to regain market share.
"The market would not view any acquisition plans by Sainsbury favourably at the moment and I think the company knows that," the sector analyst said.
Sainsbury dealt a blow to its shares and the market in January when it warned profits would be hit by the cost of improving sales.
It continues to try to regain market share lost when Tesco tipped it off the top slot just over a year ago.
Its shares were up 5-1/2 pence to 313-1/2 pence as the market assumed it would not be putting Littlewoods stores on its shopping list.
Safeway, which declined to comment on the Littlewoods announcement, also saw its shares gain, rising eight pence to 373 pence, as analysts felt it would defer from any moves outside food selling.
"I feel any acquisition by Safeway would have to focus on food and the stores on offer are not all appropriate," the analyst said.

Financing could be the dampener to any interest from frozen food retailer Iceland Group Plc, analysts said, with market capitalisation of 250 million pounds or so making a bid of double that size "audacious in the extreme," according to the sector analyst.
But Iceland has already chalked up its interest when it made a joint bid of 1.1 billion pounds for the whole group in 1995 in conjunction with home shopping company N. Brown.
Littlewoods shareholders rejected all bids for the company at that time.
"Financing could be difficult this time around for Iceland and there is no guarantee N. Brown would go with them," the analyst said.
"I think all the food retailers should have a look at the Littlewoods stores but the focus is clearly on Tesco and ASDA," he added. ($ = 0.619 British Pounds)
